dft_0K_clamped_ion_stress_strain_full_Ci.method: QE finite strain ±0.005, 12 SCF (6 Voigt patterns × ±h), full 6×6 Cij extracted from stress tensor σ = -(1/V) ∂E/∂ε with QE sign flip. Off-diagonal C12/C13/C23 measured directly via the column-by-column approach (one strain SCF gives one Cij column). No external bulk modulus K needed.
dft_0K_clamped_ion_stress_strain_full_Ci.advantage_over_energy_method: Energy curvature only recovers diagonal Voigt C_ii. Stress-strain gives the full 6×6 matrix in the same 12 SCFs, including the off-diagonal cross-coupling, with a built-in cross-check (Cij = Cji symmetry).

dft_0K_relaxed_ion_stress_strain_full_Ci.method: Same 12 strain SCFs (±0.005, 6 Voigt) but with atoms ALLOWED TO RELAX at each fixed strained cell (calculation='relax', cell_dofree='none' implicit, BFGS conv_thr 1e-4 Ry/au). Stress measured AT the relaxed atomic positions → includes ionic Born screening. Compared to clamped-ion which freezes atoms at V0 positions.
dft_0K_relaxed_ion_stress_strain_full_Ci.vacancy_paradox_role: Clamped-ion DFT systematically over-estimates argyrodite elastic moduli (E_VRH 52.31 GPa for LPSCl vs experiment ~23 GPa, ~2.3× too stiff). Allowing ion relaxation recovers experimentally consistent values. This is the physics behind why the 'clamped-ion vacancy paradox' (LPSCl ≈ LPSCl1.6 elastically at static 0K) needs finite-T or relaxed-ion to resolve.

intrinsic_vs_extrinsic._UPDATE_kim2025: Refined by Kim ACS Mater. Lett. 2025 (see literature_kim_2025_halogen_modulus): the Cl-rich stiffening is NOT only extrinsic GB pinning — it is ALSO intrinsic (Cl smaller anion -> higher ion-packing density -> higher Young's E), and our RELAXED-ION DFT already captures it (modelc E 27.66 > comp1 22.06, +24%). The clamped-ion 'identical E' (line 48) was a frozen-framework baseline that created the APPARENT paradox; the physical relaxed-ion E resolves it and agrees with Kim's Cl->E up trend.

literature_kim_2025_halogen_modulus._paper: Young Jung Kim, Sahn Nahm, Jong-Ho Lee, Hyoungchul Kim, 'Comprehensive Analysis of Halogen-Rich Argyrodite Sulfides from a Multi-Level Perspective: Li-Ion Conduction and Elastic Modulus', ACS Materials Lett. 2025, 7, 724-729. DOI 10.1021/acsmaterialslett.4c02029. FULL PDF read 2026-06-08. (Mechanical paper #4 in the group weekly report.)
literature_kim_2025_halogen_modulus.system: Li7-zPS6-zCl(z-x)Brx (AZBrX), 1.0<=z<=1.6, 0<=x<=1.6, 42 compositions. The x=0 (pure-Cl) edge is EXACTLY our comp1 (z=1, Li6PS5Cl) -> modelc (z=1.6, Li5.4PS4.4Cl1.6) series.
literature_kim_2025_halogen_modulus.method: sigma_Li by EIS; E by ultrasonic pulse-echo (UPE) on pellets pressed at 370 MPa (= PELLET/microstructure Young's modulus, not single-crystal). Two sets: BM-AZBrX (ball-milled, low crystallinity, partial argyrodite) and HT-AZBrX (heat-treated 500C/2h, high crystallinity).

key_trends.Cl_up_E_up: Increasing Cl content -> HIGHER Young's E (stiffer), pronounced in crystalline HT samples ('E increased sharply'). Cl- (167 pm) smaller than S2- -> higher ion-packing density -> stiffer.
key_trends.Br_up_E_down: Increasing Br -> LOWER E (softer); Br- (182 pm) larger -> more free volume / lower packing density -> E down to 12.59 GPa (BM). Matches OUR DFT comp-series 'Br up -> E down'.
key_trends.crystallinity: Heat treatment (crystallinity) raises E ~25% (BM 12-17 GPa -> HT 15-22 GPa) and raises sigma_Li (up to 9.9 mS/cm, 4.9x BM). The HT increase is largely microstructural (denser, better-crystallized pellet).
key_trends.sigma_drivers: High sigma_Li needs total halogen z>=1.4 AND Cl-rich (smaller radius); also anion (Cl/Br) site disorder helps. Optimized region for ASSB = low E (<=18 GPa) + high sigma (>=8 mS/cm) = mixed-halogen + specific Cl (where anion disorder AND low packing density coexist).

literature_kim_2025_halogen_modulus.RESOLVES_our_vacancy_paradox: Kim's experimental 'Cl -> E up' (Young's) CONFIRMS our DFT RELAXED-ION result (modelc E_VRH 27.66 > comp1 22.06, +24%; shear-dominant G +28%) — see dft_0K_relaxed_ion_stress_strain_full_Cij headline 'VACANCY PARADOX RESOLVED'. The apparent paradox came from the CLAMPED-ion comparison (E identical 52.31=52.30, frozen PS4 framework). Physically, when ions relax (Born screening), the Cl-rich vacancy + 4d-Cl anti-site disorder JAMS soft shear configurations -> higher G/E. So: (i) clamped-ion identical = unchanged PS4 bonding framework (consistent with our ELF/COHP/Bader); (ii) relaxed-ion modelc stiffer = the real Young's modulus, matching Kim. Modulus type matters: E and G are HIGHER for Cl-rich (shear, our relaxed-ion + Kim), while BULK B0 is LOWER for Cl-rich (our EOS 21.7 < 26.2; more Li vacancy = easier hydrostatic compression). Quote the right modulus for the right claim.
literature_kim_2025_halogen_modulus.absolute_value_context: Kim UPE E (pellet) 15-22 GPa (HT) / 12-17 (BM); our AFM (weekly report) LPSCl1.6 14.9 GPa, NdO-LPSCl1.6 15.8 GPa; our DFT relaxed-ion E 22-28 GPa (ideal single crystal, upper bound). Real pellets are softer than ideal crystal (porosity/GB), so DFT > UPE > nothing-contradictory. TREND (Cl-rich stiffer in E/G) consistent across DFT relaxed-ion, Kim UPE, and our AFM direction (NdO doping 14.9->15.8).
literature_kim_2025_halogen_modulus.relevance_to_group: Kim's chemo-mechanical map (low-E + high-sigma optimization) directly supports the Hyundai coating-layer design goal (low modulus + high oxidation stability electrolyte = NdO-LPSC) in the weekly report.

literature_kim_JMCA_2026_Irich._paper: Young Jung Kim, Sahn Nahm, Jae Jin Kim, Jong-Ho Lee, Hyoungchul Kim, 'Tailoring I-rich argyrodite sulfides via low-energy mechanical alloying for all-solid-state Li-metal batteries', J. Mater. Chem. A 2026, 14, 9939-9947. DOI 10.1039/d5ta10262f. FULL PDF read 2026-06-08. (Mechanical paper #5 in the group weekly report — the LAST literature paper.)
literature_kim_JMCA_2026_Irich.system: Li5.4PS4.6Cl1.4-xIx (LMA-Cl1.4-xIx), 0<=x<=1.4 (Cl->I substitution). LMA = low-energy mechanical alloying (30 G) vs HMA = high-energy (49 G). Anode-side focus (Li metal + LiI SEI).
literature_kim_JMCA_2026_Irich.halide_size_modulus_CONFIRMS_ours: Cl->I substitution: E DECREASES with I content, minimum 10.68 GPa. 'The lower E can be attributed to the substitution of smaller Cl- (167 pm) with larger I- (220 pm), which expands lattice free volume and reduces ion-packing density.' SAME packing-density / free-volume mechanism as Kim 2025 (Br) and our DFT comp-series (Br up -> E down). Establishes the general rule: LARGER halide -> more free volume -> LOWER E (softer); SMALLER Cl -> stiffer. Reinforces that our intrinsic DFT correctly captures the halide-size->modulus physics.
literature_kim_JMCA_2026_Irich.optimal_composition: LMA-Cl0.8I0.6 (Li5.4PS4.6Cl0.8I0.6): sigma_Li 2.44 mS/cm (highest among I-rich), E 12.37 GPa (moderate/low), critical current density 1.6 mA/cm2, 99% capacity retention after 250 cycles at 1C. LMA (partial crystallization + amorphous) balances sigma & E; HMA over-crystallizes I-rich -> ordered LPSI -> LOW sigma (inter-cage jumps suppressed).
literature_kim_JMCA_2026_Irich.anode_interface_mechanism: I-rich forms a LiI-based SEI -> uniform Li+/e- distribution -> suppresses dendrites, lowers interfacial resistance growth (R_i-3 +49% over 100 cyc for Cl0.8I0.6 vs +216% in 40 cyc for I1.4). Low E -> conformal Li contact. XPS/ToF-SIMS: framework P-/PS-/S- decrease, byproducts Li3P-/LiS-/LiI- increase on cycling.
literature_kim_JMCA_2026_Irich.relevance_to_group: An ALTERNATIVE low-modulus route (Cl->I, larger halide) to the group's NdO-doping coating strategy. Confirms the design lever 'larger halide / more free volume -> softer E' for the Hyundai low-modulus coating layer. NOTE: I-substitution lowers E AND targets the ANODE (Li-metal/LiI SEI), whereas the group's NdO-LPSC coating targets the CATHODE side (low E + high oxidation stability). Different interface, same low-E design principle.
literature_kim_JMCA_2026_Irich.vs_our_modelc: Their pure-Cl end LMA-Cl1.4 (Li5.4PS4.6Cl1.4) is close to our modelc (Li5.4PS4.4Cl1.6); both are the STIFFEST of the halide series (E ~16 GPa pellet, since E falls with I). Consistent with our Cl-rich = stiffer (E/G) finding.
